geometryValidation.notes: Targeted generation/import/exact regeneration, asset integrity, strict LOD/material budgets and source/imported normals/winding/UVs pass. Imported controls verify nine sloping sill tops at two depths, solid front thickness, all close vertical bar fronts/inward sides, transverse bars, air between bars and opaque glazing behind them. Retained court remains open and original mapped roof remains present. Controls2/29/29/137 pass. Original map/terrain hashes retained; no unchanged finished model regenerated or blanket revalidated.

limitations: Original medium-fi surviving compound exterior. Current window construction uses the exact2009 B-section native original already cleared as public domain in Qualla, with the named creator release and original upload log verified. Earlier attribution-licensed imagery is excluded as current control; other compound elevations remain inherited mapped approximations.

Nine windows on one retained mapped courtyard facade now have solid security bars at close range and physical sloping red sills from district onward. The B-section photograph controls visible treatment; exact photo-to-court/window identity, metric sections, spacing and present condition remain estimates. Other facades retain generalized window geometry.
Four H-blocks, main open courtyards, service buildings and five watchtowers retain their mapped layout. Main roof segmentation, smaller courtyard walls and hidden facade details are interpretations.

Heights, window spacing beyond the photographed entrance and B-section, fence bays and rooftop equipment are photographic estimates. Irregular blue-stone cladding is generalized using authored polygons and shared basalt.
Roof uses a matte corrugated shared surface to represent the observed pale cement sheets; it is not evidence that the original roof is metal.
Kramat, graveyard, other prisons, interiors, exhibits, furnishings and vegetation are excluded. No reference-image pixels are embedded.

Independent terrain is preserved. Whole blocks and towers use fixed locally sampled floor elevations; fences follow the sampled slope. These inferred levels are not a survey, and exact ground contact can differ on another host elevation dataset.
